transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I just can’t sit still in these meetings or trainings anymore. I feel like I’ve got to get up and move even when everyone else is fine staying put.
Did this restlessness start recently, perhaps after beginning a new medication, or is this something you have struggled with since childhood?

It’s actually been a lifelong thing, though it’s gotten much worse since my promotion a year and a half ago. My mom still talks about how my grade school teachers constantly called her because I couldn’t stay in my seat and kept wandering around the room. So I’ve definitely struggled with this since I was a kid.
Along with this physical restlessness, do you find yourself constantly plagued by excessive, uncontrollable worries about everyday things like your work performance, family, or health?

No, I wouldn't say I'm plagued by constant worries or anxiety like that. It's really more of a physical thing—this constant, buzzing need to move my body or fidget, rather than my mind racing with worry.
Along with the physical restlessness, do you also struggle with focusing on tasks, organizing your work, or frequently losing things?

To be honest, I don't really struggle with losing things or organizing my work. My main issue is just the physical restlessness and that constant, driving need to keep moving, rather than a lack of focus.
Do you often find yourself acting on impulse, such as interrupting others when they are talking or having a hard time waiting your turn?

Yes, that is a major issue for me. In staff briefings, I constantly cut people off and blurt out answers before my supervisor even finishes asking, which often leads to me misunderstanding them. I also find it incredibly hard to wait my turn, whether I'm in a meeting, standing in line at the supply office, or even playing bingo with my wife.
Do these difficulties with restlessness and interrupting others cause significant problems or strain in your relationships at home or with your performance at work?

Yes, they've caused real problems both at work and at home. On the job, my restlessness and interrupting have led to me messing up our scheduling system, missing training details, and getting written up after complaints from building managers. At home, it's caused arguments with my wife because I just can't sit still through church or bingo nights like I promised.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a lifelong history of severe physical restlessness, inability to remain seated, fidgeting, and impulsivity (interrupting others, difficulty waiting turn) dating back to childhood. These symptoms cause significant impairment in both occupational and social/marital functioning. The patient denies prominent inattention symptoms (such as losing things or disorganization) and excessive worries, which rules out the combined type of ADHD (F90.2) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1), confirming the diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive type (F90.1).
